Use case: illustration-story. Production comic panel for the original fantasy card game BOBOZAN, Crown War prologue. Landscape 3:2 composition, full-bleed single illustration, no surrounding panel frame. Art direction: tactile hand-cut woodblock / linocut fantasy adventure illustration with fine micro-pixel stepped contours and discreet engraved stipple; large confident dark ink shapes, strongly readable silhouettes, charming stylized proportions, restrained print texture. Limited rich palette: midnight navy and deep teal shadows, copper/chestnut architecture, pale parchment highlights and warm amber light, touches of muted scarlet. Not photorealistic, not a 3D render, no airbrushed digital-painting finish. Consistent original world of small anthropomorphic fantasy villagers and little clockwork robots. No lettering, no words, no symbols that look like text, no speech balloons, no UI, no card border, no watermark. Narration will be added in HTML outside this image. Meaningful dramatic story composition, not an environment texture or gameplay battlefield.
Panel 1, THE NIGHT THE TOWN LOST: Wide establishing shot from street level across a humble cobblestone village square at blue dusk. Small timber houses with glowing amber windows and hanging lanterns. On the left foreground a weary small turtle villager carrying a drooping muted-red tournament pennant (simple lantern pictogram, no writing), beside two other tiny dejected animal villagers returning home. All are peaceful and unharmed. On the right middle ground a tall dark crowned clockwork collector silhouette approaches, carrying an unlit metal collection case. Far up the hill beyond the roofs, a huge aloof Crown citadel glows golden under a storm-blue sky. A single town street lantern with a golden core is an obvious visual anchor near the center. The citadel appears powerful, the town vulnerable. Keep the number of villagers low (3), foreground shapes broad, upper sky quieter, composition immediately readable at small size. Strong storytelling comic framing.

Panel 2, THE LIGHT IS TAKEN: Very dramatic comic close-up, diagonally framed. A huge blackened brass articulated mechanical collector hand with a small angular crown seal on its wrist reaches in from the UPPER RIGHT and pulls a brilliant amber faceted light core out of an open iron town lantern at center-left. The core is separated clearly from its circular socket by a few inches; a short trail of gold sparks marks the moment of removal. This is the same original cold Crown collector: black angular machinery with brass edge accents, no human hand. Behind the hand, a row of humble chestnut timber houses recedes into deep midnight-blue shadows; three small windows go dark. At the lower left edge the silhouette of a little turtle villager watches, very small compared with the hand. One sharply glowing amber light source illuminates the metal fingers and empty lamp socket. Strong black shapes and amber-white focal point, minimal background detail, slightly pixel-stepped engraved woodcut edges, rich flat-print grain. The entire image must be completely free of text and captions.

Panel 3, A SEAT IS STILL OPEN: Intimate medium close-up inside the humble Emberwick tavern after the town's street lights have been seized. Our friendly guide Axle, an original small chunky BLUE robot, is on the LEFT/CENTER leaning over a wooden table and extending an ENTRY CARD toward the viewer in his right metal hand. The card is clearly blank parchment except for a SINGLE simple small lantern pictogram (no letters or numbers). Axle has a rounded square blue-metal helmet, a large black rectangular face screen with TWO vertical glowing yellow eyes, round silver side earpieces, one short antenna with amber tip, a teal segmented torso and small glowing round amber chest core. No mouth. He looks warmly determined through his slight head tilt. Character proportions compact and charming like a small toy automaton; stylize him in the same engraved woodcut ink shapes as the surroundings, not smooth 3D metal. His offered hand and card are the central foreground focal point with tasteful foreshortening. On the right side of the table: a rolled travel map with simple unlabeled paths, a worn canvas satchel, three blank circular wax seal impressions arranged like a journey. Background a dark cozy timber-and-brick tavern, one tiny hearth glow, shelves suggested in large quiet ink blocks. The player is the camera: no visible protagonist, no fixed human hands or player face. Warm amber invitation amid navy night shadows, hope in an uncertain place. No text of any kind, no UI.

Panel 4, THE ROAD TO THREE SEALS: Sweeping hopeful wide shot looking UP a winding stone approach toward an original great Crown arena gate, angular round amphitheater with huge crown-shaped spires glowing under a pale-gold horizon and deep blue dawn clouds. A small unknown hooded traveler, seen only as a back silhouette in the lower center, walks UP the road away from the viewer. Keep the silhouette avatar-agnostic: face, skin and species fully concealed by travel cloak, no human hand showing. The roadside is lined by exactly THREE prominent regional standards, each simple and readable: one muted vermilion banner with a cream claw pictogram, one deep jade banner with a cream shield pictogram, one dark amethyst banner with a cream crescent-and-three-dots pictogram. They signify different card-playing guilds, not all fire. A narrow golden stream of stolen light runs in inset channels along the citadel bridge toward the central high tower, quietly hinting that its power comes from elsewhere. Near lower edge a last tiny lantern with a weak warm light, recalling the hometown. Distinct foreground / road / arena depth, clear large carved-print shapes, simple atmospheric shapes rather than realistic mountains, image readable as the fourth page of the same woodcut comic. No captions, lettering, words, numbers, UI, or border.
